slides.headline: The most trafficked mammal on Earth is one you've never seen.
The only mammal covered in scales
slides.body: Eight species across Africa and Asia. The scales are keratin, the same material as your fingernails. When threatened, a pangolin rolls into an armoured ball.

slides.label: how far a large pangolin's tongue can extend
slides.body: It has no teeth at all. The tongue is anchored deep in the chest, near the pelvis in some species, and is coated in sticky saliva.

slides.headline: It eats with its stomach, not its mouth
slides.body: A pangolin can eat well over 100 g of ants and termites a day. With no teeth, it swallows small stones and grinds the insects in a muscular, gizzard-like stomach.

slides.label: estimated to have been trafficked in a single decade
slides.body: Mostly for scales used in traditional medicine and for meat. Three species (Chinese, Sunda and Philippine) are Critically Endangered.
slides.source: Challender et al. (2014); IUCN Red List

slides.headline: All trade is banned. Poaching isn't over.
slides.body: Since 2017 all eight species sit on CITES Appendix I, which bans international commercial trade. Enforcement, not the law, is now the bottleneck.

slides.headline: Send this to someone who's never seen one.
slides.body: Awareness is the first step. Follow @claudes_plan101 for more.

caption:
Pangolins are the only mammals with scales, and the most trafficked mammals on Earth.

No teeth, a tongue up to 40 cm, and a stomach that grinds ants with swallowed stones. Eight species; three are Critically Endangered, and international commercial trade in all of them has been banned under CITES Appendix I since 2017.

Swipe through, then send this to someone who's never seen one.

Sources: IUCN Red List; CITES; Challender et al. (2015). Photos: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (credits on each slide).
